Enantioselective Construction of 1 H‑Isoindoles Containing Tri- and
Diﬂuoromethylated Quaternary Stereogenic Centers via Palladium-
Catalyzed C −H Bond Imidoylation
Jian Wang, * Lianjie Li, Minxue Chai, Shumin Ding, Jing Li, Yongjia Shang, * Haixia Zhao, Dan Li,
and Qiang Zhu *
Cite This: ACS Catal. 2021, 11, 12367 −12374 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: An intermolecular enantioselective synthesis of 1 H-
isoindoles containing tri- and di ﬂuoromethylated quaternary
stereogenic centers through a palladium-catalyzed desymmetric
C−H bond imidoylation has been developed. α,α-Diaryl tri- and
diﬂuoroethylated isocyanides acted as powerful precursors of chiral
1H-isoindoles, in which the ﬂuoroalkyl group was proven to play a
crucial role in both the stereochemistry and reaction e ﬃciency. In
addition, an allene insertion cascade was realized, o ﬀering rapid
access to diverse C1-tethered bis-heterocyclic sca ﬀolds with good yields and high enantioselectivities. The reactions proceeded
smoothly under mild conditions with low catalyst loadings.
KEYWORDS: tri- and di ﬂuoromethylated quaternary stereogenic center, 1H-isoindole, palladium, imidoylation,
enantioselective C −H activation
O
rganic compounds incorporated with ﬂuorine atoms
have witnessed broad applications in agro- and medicinal
chemistry.1 The solubility, lipophilicity, binding a ﬃnity, and
metabolic stability of drug candidates can be signi ﬁcantly
altered due to the unique electronic and steric properties of
ﬂuoroalkyl moieties. A di ﬂuoromethyl group (CF 2H) with an
acidic C −H bond can play the role of a lipophilic hydrogen-
bond donor and a bioisostere of alcohols and thiols in drug
design.
2 In addition to ﬂuoroalkylarenes,3 tri- and di ﬂuor-
omethylated stereogenic centers frequently occur in pharma-
ceuticals and lead compounds ( Figure 1 a) and the catalytic
construction of such stereocenters has attracted much
attention from the synthetic community.
4 In this regard,
asymmetric functionalization of prochiral ﬂuoroalkylated
compounds is one of the most important categories. 5 For
instance, the use of catalytic enantioselective addition reactions
of ﬂuoroalkyl ketones,
6 ketoimines,7 and Michael acceptors 8
was proven to be a powerful strategy for the synthesis of
enantioenriched ﬂuoroalkylated alcohols and amines. Another
well-established approach is the transformation of α-triﬂuor-
omethyl carbanions, which have traditionally su ﬀered from the
side reaction of β-ﬂuoro elimination. 9 Overall, the reported
successful strategies 10 mostly relied on transformations of
substrates containing unsaturated double bonds and were
mainly limited to tri ﬂuoromethyl compounds. The construc-
tion of di ﬂuoromethylated stereogenic centers has been far less
investigated, and only a few examples have been reported. 11
Furthermore, the synthesis of complex molecules with
switchable CF
3-o rC F 2H-containing stereogenic centers by
using the same synthetic method has been even more rarely
developed.12
The isoindole core is ubiquitous in bioactive molecules and
natural products. 13 Although a variety of catalytic enantiose-
lective methods have been developed to access isoindo-
lines
14−18 and isoindolones 19−22 (reduced and oxidized
isoindoles) by the groups of Enders, 14 Sasai,15 Gong,16
Jarvo,17 Wang,18 Matsunaga,19 Cramer,20 Nishimura,21 and
Wang22 and others, the synthesis of 1 H-isoindoles has mostly
been con ﬁned to racemic versions. 23 In 2018, Cramer and co-
workers developed the ﬁrst Pd(0)-catalyzed intramolecular C −
H bond imidoylation reaction to a ﬀord 1 H-isoindoles with
quaternary stereogenic centers ( Figure 1 b).24 The enantiose-
lective C −H bond activation 25 strategy utilized tri ﬂuorometh-
yl-substituted imid oyl chlorides as internal electrophiles.
Herein, we report an intermolecular protocol for the
construction of 1 H-isoindoles bearing both tri- and di ﬂuor-
omethylated quaternary stereogenic centers through palla-
dium-catalyzed C −H bond imidoylation.
26 α,α-Diaryl tri- and
diﬂuoroethylated isocyanides were utilized as coupling partners
of aryl and alkenyl iodides, o ﬀering access to diverse 1 H-

isoindoles in high yields and enantioselectivities (up to 99%
yield and 99% ee) ( Figure 1 c). Furthermore, several kinds of
C1-tethered bis-heterocyclic sca ﬀolds were enantioselectively
accessed through an allene insertion cascade. The reactions
proceeded smoothly under mild conditions with low catalyst
loadings. Control experiments revealed that the ﬂuoroalkyl
group might play a crucial role in the stereochemistry and
reaction e ﬃciency.
The study was initiated by employing (2,2,2-tri ﬂuoro-1-
isocyanoethane-1,1-diyl)dibenzene (1a) and iodobenzene ( 2a)
as model substrates. When 1a was added dropwise via a syringe
pump over 2 h, the racemic product 3a was generated in 97%
yield under the catalysis of Pd(OAc)
2 (10 mol %) and PPh 3
(20 mol %) with Cs 2CO3 (1.0 equiv) and PivOH (0.6 equiv)
as additives ( Table 1 , entry 1). Next, chiral phosphoramidite
ligands L1−L3 were tested for asymmetric catalysis (entries 2 −
4), and product 3a was formed in 94% yield and 98% ee with
the SPINOL-derived phosphoramidite ligand L3 (entry 4).
When bidentate BINAP was used as the ligand, both the
eﬃciency and enantioselectivity of the reaction obviously
decreased (entry 5). Other palladium catalysts such as PdCl 2
and Pd 2(dba)3 resulted in lower yields of 60% and 49%,
respectively (entries 6 and 7). Satisfyingly, when 1 mol % of
catalyst was used, the product was delivered in 93% yield and
97% ee (entry 9). The enantioselectivity decreased to 89% by
using bromobenzene as an electrophilic coupling partner of 1a
(entry 10).
With the optimized conditions in hand, the scope for the
construction of 1 H-isoindoles containing tri ﬂuoromethylated
stereogenic centers was ﬁrst investigated ( Scheme 1 ). Screen-
ing of functional groups on the aryl iodides revealed that both
electron-donating (Me,
tBu, and OMe) and electron-with-
drawing (F, Cl, Br, CF 3,C O2Me, CHO, CN, and NO 2) groups
were well tolerated. The corresponding products 3a−u were
generated in high yields and enantioselectivities. When the
reaction was conducted with 1-iodo-2-methylbenzene as the
coupling partner, 2-methylated product 3b was obtained in
90% yield and 89% ee, suggesting that the enantioselectivity
was slightly in ﬂuenced by steric hindrance. Notably, the C −Br
bond remained stable under the applied conditions and
bromosubstituted products 3n,o were obtained in 97% yield
with 98% ee and 94% yield with 96% ee, respectively, which
could facilitate further transformations. Naphthyl- and
heteroaryl-substituted products 3v−x were also obtained in
high yields and ee. In addition, alkenyl iodides could act as
eﬃcient electrophilic coupli ng partners with a slightly
improved catalyst loading of 5 mol %, a ﬀording alkenylated
1H-isoindoles 3y,z in good yields and high enantioselectivities.

Next, the scope of isocyanides was tested under the standard
conditions. Substituents such as Me, OMe, F, Cl, and Br were
all well tolerated. Products 3aa−ae were obtained in 80 −99%
yields and 96 −98% ee. A gram-scale preparation of 3a was
conducted without loss of e ﬃciency.
Then our attention switched to the study of construction of
CF
2H-containing stereocenters ( Scheme 1 ). When (2,2-
diﬂuoro-1-isocyanoethane-1,1-diyl)dibenzene 1 was reacted
with iodobenzene 2a under the standard conditions, the
desired product 4a was generated in only 43% yield and 87%
ee, with a large amount of isocyanide remaining unreacted. To
our delight, the yield and enantioselectivity were improved to
95% and 92%, respectively, by increasing the catalyst loading to
5 mol %. The e ﬃcient synthesis of CF
2H-containing chiral 1H-
isoindoles was developed by investigating aryl iodides with
various functional groups such as Me,
tBu, OMe, Ph, F, Cl, Br,
CF3,C O 2Me, CHO, CN, and NO 2. Aryl- and heteroarylated
1H-isoindoles 4a−w were generated in high yields and ee.
Alkenylated products 4x,y were obtained in 77% yield with
97% ee and 24% yield with 96% ee, respectively. The low yield
of 4y was attributed to the generation of the imidic pivalic
anhydride 4y′ as a major byproduct. The isocyanide substrates
with F, Cl ,and Br functional groups reacted smoothly, and
cyclization products 4z−ab were generated in 80 −91% yield
and 93 −98% ee.
Next, we examined the reactivity of isocyanide insertion into
the allyl-palladium intermediate, which was generated by
intramolecular allene insertion ( Scheme 2a). Satisfyingly, when
allene substrates 5a−c were subjected to the reaction with a
catalyst loading of 10 mol %, C1-tethered benzofuran/indole/
isoquinolinone-isoindole bisheterocyclic sca ﬀolds 6a−c were
generated in 54 −84% yields and 98 −99% ee.
To further demonstrate the utility of this reaction, we tested
enantioselective C −H imidoylation with aryl iodides derived
from natural products (menthol, tyrosine, and estrone), a dye
(BODIPY), and drug molecules ( Scheme 2 b). The products
were uniformly obtained in good yields with high enantiomeric
(7g; 65% yield and 85% ee) and diastereomeric ( 7a−f,h;7 2−
99% yields and 89 −99% de) excesses. Then the trans-
formations of 3a were carried out as exempli ﬁed in Scheme
2c. Selective mono- and dinitration reactions were successfully
performed, delivering 8a,b in 56% and 52% yields, respectively.
The chirality remained stable under the applied conditions.
To shed light on the stereochemical outcomes of the
cyclization reaction, a control experiment with methylated
isocyanide 9 as the substrate was carried out under the
standard conditions ( Scheme 3 a). The imidoylation product

10 was obtained in only 11% yield and 57% ee, suggesting that
the ﬂuoroalkyl group might play a crucial role in both the
enantioselectivity control and the reaction e ﬃciency of the
desymmetric C −H imidoylation. On the basis of previous
reports,27 a plausible C −H···F−C hydrogen-bond e ﬀect27c−e is
preliminarily depicted in Scheme 3 b.
In summary, we have developed an enantioselective
palladium-catalyzed C −H bond imidoylation for the con-
struction of 1 H-isoindoles containing tri- and di ﬂuoromethy-
lated quaternary stereogenic centers with α,α-diaryl tri- and
diﬂuoroethyl isocyanides as coupling partners of aryl and
alkenyl iodide derivatives. A variety of chiral 1 H-isoindoles
were synthesized in good yields (up to 99% yield) and
enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). This intermolecular
protocol is also compatible with various aryl iodides bearing
core structures of natural products, a dye, and drug molecules.
In addition, diverse C1-tethered bis-heterocyclic sca ﬀolds were
aﬀorded in good yields and high enantioselectivities through an
allene insertion cascade. The reactions were carried out under
mild conditions with low catalyst loadings. A bioactive
evaluation of the chiral products is currently underway in
our laboratory.
